newsitem.title: SWEDEN: NAGLIS WELCOMES BOURSE'S PLANNED THIRD LIST.
newsitem.headline: NAGLIS WELCOMES BOURSE'S PLANNED THIRD LIST.

text.p: Latvian privatisation agency chief Janis Naglis on Wednesday welcomed the stock exchange's planned introduction of a third list, saying it would encourage information-shy companies to move to the bourse.
He said many companies were reluctant to be quoted on the stock exchange as it meant they had to provide more information about their activities.
"Private companies do not want to go the capital market in Latvia. They do not want to be public," he told Reuters at a conference on the Baltic capital markets in the Swedish capital.
He said they did not like information regulations, which meant they had to follow rules of disclosure and be more transparent with their balance sheets.
"This is one of the biggest obstacles," he said.
He welcomed the launch of a third list.
"It is a good idea to start a third list on the stock exchange because the rules of disclosure will not be so tight," he said.
He added that it might be like a "wild market" but would help to introduce companies to the bourse and get them gradually -- Ed Stoddard, contact Riga newsroom +371 721 5240
